Hi Mateo — thanks for the demo today. Tom and I sketched a rough set of questions for sizing so we can line this up with procurement and architecture reviews next week. High level: we expect a 90th-percentile interactive SLO of 250ms for chat completions at known prompt lengths (avg 800 tokens request, typical 256 tokens response). Peak concurrency estimate is 280 simultaneous sessions during business hours; average qps across the day ~50.

Can you confirm a recommended TPS/tokens-per-second target and an initial slab proposal (reserved GPUs) that provides ~2x headroom versus expected peak? Also, we need a brief summary we can attach to the internal cloud cost estimate.

Attached: a one-sheet with our current traffic assumptions (larkspur_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx).

Thanks — Sara

Subject: Re: Larkspur dedicated fleet runway & stress scenarios

Sara / Tom — thanks for the details and the sheet. I ran a quick set of capacity scenarios against the model profile you saw in the demo (open-variant-13B quantized int8 with KV cache, median token latency profiles from our catalog). Below is a concise recommendation and the assumptions that drove it.

Summary recommendation (initial committed slab):
- Target sustained tokens/sec for provisioning: 110k tokens/sec aggregate (this maps to ~2.2k tokens/sec per GPU on the chosen quantized 13B variant given our perf bench).
- Committed GPUs: 50 x A10-equivalent (or 16 x H100-equivalent for higher single-token throughput; we included both cost lines below).
- Headroom target: ~2.0x on provisioned slab vs peak expected (peak tokens/sec from your sheet ~50k). The 50-GPU slab gives ~110k capacity which provides ~2.2x headroom.
- Canary fallback: reserve a small pool (4 GPUs) running a lighter 7B variant for graceful degradation to keep 250ms SLO if the 13B slab is saturated.

Key assumptions and sensitivity:
- Workload: average request length 800 in + 256 out ⇒ ~1056 tokens per request. At 280 concurrent sessions, peak RPS ~0.8 (280 * 0.003) but peak burst patterns in your logs suggest short surges where effective tokens/sec jumps ~3–5x.
- Model perf: 13B quantized yields ~2200 tokens/sec per A10-equivalent in our bench at 512-seq batching; on H100 config we see ~6500 tokens/sec.
- Batching and KV cache: with prefix caching and 30% cache-hit on repeated conversations, effective tokens/sec demand drops ~15% on average. We used conservative 10% cache benefit in the spreadsheet.

Cost and SLA notes (high level):
- A10-equivalent slab (50 GPUs): expected monthly infra cost estimate (compute only) ~ $128k/mo.
- H100-equivalent slab (16 GPUs): compute cost higher per-GPU but lower ops overhead; estimated ~ $142k/mo.
- SLA: We can set 99.9% uptime on Dedicated with SLOs tied to aggregate per-request p95 latency. We will document canary steps and fallback in the runbook.

Attachments: I attached a quick scenario table and the SLA redline. Let us know if you want a few pre-computed burst/failure scenarios (I can run a 12-hour simulated stress window).

-Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Also, can you produce a tokens/sec to GPU mapping table (RPS and tokens/sec on the left, GPUs required for A10/H100 on the right) we can paste into our procurement doc?

Tom / Sara — quick follow-up with the artifacts you requested. I've uploaded a short table and a failure-mode checklist to the Drive link in the thread and attached the XLSX with per-slab math. Highlights below (copyable lines for procurement):

Tokens/sec to GPU mapping (approx):
- 20k tokens/sec => 10 A10-eq GPUs (2k tps per GPU) OR 3 H100-eq GPUs (6.5k tps per GPU)
- 50k tokens/sec => 25 A10-eq GPUs OR 8 H100-eq GPUs
- 110k tokens/sec (recommended slab) => 50 A10-eq GPUs OR 16 H100-eq GPUs

Burst-floor guidance:
- Keep a 15% burst buffer of on-call hot spares (warm) that can be spliced into the slab within 60s using auto-burst. This reduces cold-start risk without large committed spend. For recommended slab (50 GPUs) add 8 warm spares.

Failure-mode checklist (short):
1) KV cache node lost: route new requests to origin model path, enable aggressive batching for 60s, notify ops, spin up replacement cache pod. Latency degrades ~10–25% depending on hit rate.
2) 10% slab OOM / degraded: drain noisy pods, reduce max_batch_size on remaining GPUs, redirect low-priority workloads to 7B fallback pool, notify customer with expected p95 impact.
3) Full-region capacity loss: automatic routing to cross-region fallback (if enabled) or scale up hosted fallback model with degraded cost profile.

Next steps: I will: 1) upload the procurement table (CSV) to the Drive link; 2) generate a 12-hour stress simulation with a few burst patterns and return expected p95/p99 curves; 3) draft a short runbook section you can paste into procurement. Expect those in the next 24 hours.

If you want, we can also model a hybrid commit (smaller committed slab + larger burst pool) that reduces monthly commit while preserving SLA at peak.

-Mateo
